plot: Odo and Mothwick follow the tale of the Chase Vault in Barbados, where lead coffins were said to move inside a cemented tomb until Lord Combermere sealed it and spread sand on the floor; the twist is that no record of it exists before 1833, but the vault has stayed empty ever since, and fresh small footprints appear by its door.

beats.say: Who did this? The coffins are scattered across the floor!
A tale told as true, from Barbados, in the early eighteen-hundreds.
Who moves heavy lead coffins inside a tomb nobody can enter?
New episode every day — subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
A ghost ship on the ice, and now a locked tomb?
That ship's bell rang us south, Odo. All the way here.
The vault sits in the churchyard of Christ Church, near Oistins.
Its door was one huge slab of stone.
Push, all of you! Six or seven men, and it barely moves!
After every burial, masons cemented that door shut again.
Most of what we know comes from tales a local rector told.
The story says a little girl was laid here in eighteen-oh-eight.
In eighteen twelve, her sister followed. Two small coffins, side by side.
That same year, their father, Thomas Chase, was laid beside them.
Roll the stone back. Mind your feet. Bring the lamp in.
When they rolled the stone away, the small coffins had moved.
Moved? But who could even get inside?
Nobody, Odo. That is exactly the problem.
The men set the coffins straight and sealed the door again.
But each time the vault was opened, the coffins had moved again.
If this goes on, no family will ever rest in here!
Word reached the governor of Barbados himself, Lord Combermere.
Then we shall be certain. Nobody enters without my seal.
The story says he attended a burial there in eighteen nineteen.
He had fine sand spread over the floor, to catch any footprint.
Then he pressed his own seal into the wet cement.
Now let us see who walks in here.
In April eighteen twenty, they broke the seals and opened it again.
The story says the coffins lay scattered. One leaned against the door.
The sand! Look at the sand. Not a single footprint!
He ordered the coffins buried elsewhere. The vault was left empty.
Floods? An earthquake? People asked. But no water marks were found.
Then something moved them. Something already inside.
Or maybe nothing moved at all. Here is the strangest part.
Nobody printed this story until eighteen thirty-three, in a travel book.
In nineteen-oh-seven, the writer Andrew Lang went looking for proof.
The burial register. The island newspapers. Not one word about coffins.
Even the rector's own versions of the tale did not match.
In two thousand eleven, an investigator stepped inside the empty vault.
The brick walls were intact. No marks from heavy coffins hitting them.
So it never happened? It was only a story?
Then why has nobody been laid in that vault ever since?
Two hundred years on, it stands empty. And nobody knows for sure.
Odo... the sand by the door. Fresh footprints. Small ones.
Next time: two girls, an English stream, and five strange photographs.
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

long.title: Sealed Tomb. Moving Coffins. Who? ⚰️ (Ep 46)
long.description:
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

"A door seven men can barely move. And still, something got in." — Odo

A tale told as true from Barbados: in the Chase Vault at Christ Church, heavy lead coffins were said to move every time the tomb was opened — even after the governor sealed it and covered the floor with sand.

Uma história contada como verdadeira em Barbados: na cripta Chase, em Christ Church, pesados caixões de chumbo se moviam sempre que o túmulo era aberto — mesmo depois que o governador o selou e cobriu o chão de areia.

"باب بالكاد يحركه سبعة رجال. ومع ذلك دخل شيء ما." — أودو

حكاية تُروى على أنها حقيقية من باربادوس: في قبو عائلة تشيس بكنيسة كرايست تشيرش، قيل إن توابيت الرصاص الثقيلة كانت تتحرك كلما فُتح القبر، حتى بعد أن ختمه الحاكم وفرش الأرض بالرمل.

fr.title: Qui a déplacé les cercueils de ce tombeau ? ⚰️ (Ep 46)
fr.description:
Selon vous, que se passe-t-il dans la prochaine partie ? Dites-le-moi en commentaire.

« Une porte que sept hommes bougent à peine. Et pourtant, quelque chose est entré. » — Odo

Un récit raconté comme vrai à la Barbade : dans le caveau Chase de Christ Church, de lourds cercueils de plomb auraient bougé à chaque ouverture — même après que le gouverneur l'a scellé et a couvert le sol de sable.

ja.description:
次のパートで何が起こると思いますか?コメントで教えてください。

「7人がかりでやっと動く扉。それでも、何かが入った。」— オド

de.title: Wer bewegte die Särge in diesem Grab? ⚰️ (Ep 46)
de.description:
Was glaubst du, passiert im nächsten Teil? Schreib es mir in die Kommentare.

„Eine Tür, die sieben Männer kaum bewegen. Und trotzdem kam etwas hinein.“ — Odo

Eine als wahr erzählte Geschichte aus Barbados: In der Chase-Gruft von Christ Church sollen sich schwere Bleisärge bei jeder Öffnung bewegt haben – selbst nachdem der Gouverneur sie versiegelt und Sand auf den Boden streuen ließ.
